elements.evidence: Rendered 12.4 now reads "Customer is subject to no restriction on soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee." The prior one-way prohibition ("shall not solicit, hire, or employ ... during the term or for twenty-four months afterward") is gone, and no other operative text imposes a solicitation restraint on Customer; 12.3 independently confirms Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment."

No non-solicitation covenant survives in either direction; 12.4 as rendered is a negative confirmation only, so there is no mutual restraint binding Vendor. (Immaterial here because the preferred level is complete.)

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with 12.4 rewritten to impose no restriction at all, no personnel scope broader than Services personnel is imposed on Customer.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the twenty-four month tail ("during the term or for twenty-four months afterward") is deleted and no duration remains to exceed 12 months.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the "regardless of how the employee applies" negation is removed and no restriction exists to which a carve-out would attach; 12.3 also preserves hiring of "any person who responds to general recruitment."

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no solicitation covenant remains, so unsolicited approaches are unrestricted.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The no-hire operator is eliminated \u2014 12.4 now affirmatively states Customer is subject to no restriction on "soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee."

reasons: The preferred checklist is a single element and it is fully met in operative language: rendered 12.4 removes the one-way, all-employee, term-plus-24-month no-hire and states that Customer is subject to no such restriction. The position is complete at the preferred level, so fallback incompleteness is irrelevant.

Minimality holds: only Section 12.4 was touched; 12.3 (favourable to Customer) is retained verbatim, no survival tail, expense language, procedure, or extra covenant was added, and the replacement is a single concise sentence rather than a broader rewrite. Converting the prohibition into an express negative confirmation is defensible because it removes the internal conflict with 12.3 without introducing new obligations on either party.

Intent is preserved: no defined term, cross-reference, or commercial mechanic is left dangling; the edit in fact cures the prior contradiction between 12.4's no-hire and Vendor's acknowledgement in 12.3 that Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment." Nothing elsewhere reimposes a solicitation restraint that would contradict the retained language.
Deterministic gates (operation applies, minimality, element coverage) are consistent with substantive review: the rendered text, not merely the comment, carries the result.

Drafting note only (not a defect): if Vendor pushes back, the fallback offered in the comment \u2014 mutual, Services-personnel-only, 12 months post-involvement, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no hiring prohibition \u2014 would need to be drafted as operative text, since none of those mutual terms currently exist in the document.
